# Pre-analysis note (committed before any real-data result table was read)

Status of this note: written after the code and the synthetic calibration, **while the core batch (`scripts/run_core_all.sh`) was
already running**. Before this note I had looked at (i) MT-Bench-human (6 models) and ~28 Arena-55k pairs to debug the search and
(ii) the synthetic runs. No threshold below was tuned on a real-data summary; the margins come from the synthetic calibration
(`scripts/04_synthetic.py`, `04b_synthetic_pflip.py`: all rows **synthetic**) and are fixed here.

## Definitions as implemented
- Estimator: BT-MLE on pair-aggregated counts, tie = half a win to each side, ridge 1e-4 on theta (`src/btlib.py`).
- Conclusion "a above b" (ordered by the fitted theta). Alteration cost: 1 comparison = 1 (delete; outcome change b-win/tie->a-win,
  a-win/tie->b-win; free-choice insertion as extension). A tie turned into a win costs 1, a win turned into a loss costs 1 (cost-2 variant = sensitivity).
- k\* = smallest alteration count for which the exact refit has theta_a - theta_b <= 0 (ties of the fitted scores count as flipped);
  it is a **verified upper bound** found by search (iterated re-linearisation, checked by Frank-Wolfe on the continuous relaxation);
  k_lin = first-order (influence) estimate without refit; gmax = largest single-alteration first-order effect on the gap;
  z = gap / SE (z_fisher: model-based; z_boot: cluster bootstrap B=500; z_boot_cmp: comparison-level bootstrap);
  F = k\* gmax / SE_boot, Q = F / z = k\* gmax / gap (SE cancels).
- Null: simulate from the fitted BT on the same graph and n_ij with the dataset tie rate (clipped to 2 min(p,1-p)), preserving the mean score of
  every pair exactly; labelled synthetic; R = 20 replicates, 300 z-stratified pairs per dataset, same estimator and search.

## Sizes (fixed)
Real data: k\*, z, Q for **all** M(M-1)/2 pairs per dataset (Arena 2016; judges 2016 each; MT-Bench 15; NBA season <= 435), both families.
Bootstrap B=500 (cluster) and B=500 (comparison), seed 0. Null R=20 x 300 pairs. Random baselines (02_random.py): 60 pairs per dataset x 300 draws x f in
{.005,.01,.02,.05,.1,.15,.2,.3,.5}. Subsampling (05_scaling.py): fractions 1/32..1, 5 draws, 40 pairs. Z-strata: [0,1),[1,2),[2,4),[4,8),[8,inf);
the **declared z-range** for all aggregate statements is z_fisher in [1,8] (below 1 the pair is not separated; above 8 the pairs are an extrapolation of the
bootstrap and the search).

## What the synthetic calibration says (synthetic BT data, M in {12,30}, N 2e3..1.28e5, density {1,.25}, tie {0,.3}; 3 reps; 11,520 pairs with 1<z<12)
- Scaling: log k\* = a + b log z + c log N + d log P: b = 1.11 (delete) / 1.13 (flip), c = 0.45 / 0.43 (theory 1 and 0.5), residual sd 0.23 / 0.20 (log).
- Q = k\* gmax / gap under correctly specified BT: delete mean log Q = -0.03 (Q ~ 0.97; 0.90 sparse-no-ties .. 1.06 dense-ties), instance-level sd of mean log Q = 0.06 within a
  configuration; flip: mean log Q = +0.21, depends on density (sparse 1.08-1.10, dense 1.28-1.35 because the capacity of the top-influence alterations is used up). So **Q is not >= 1** under exact refit
  (the brief's inequality holds for the linear regime only) and its baseline depends on graph and family: Q is only read against its own null (same graph).
- First-order search: k_lin / k_ver median 1.26 (delete; first-order overestimates because influence grows as data is removed), 0.97 (flip).
- Random-deletion flip probability conditional on the observed sample: P_flip(f) = Phi(-z sqrt((1-f)/f)) (RMSE 0.010 over 5,000+ cells), **not** the Brief's Phi(-z sqrt(1-f))
  (RMSE 0.070, biased -0.036). Consequence: the noise-equivalent fraction f_q = z^2/(z^2 + c_q^2), c_q = |Phi^-1(q)|, is below 0.8 only for z < ~2 at q=16%.
- Search quality on 53 tiny problems (M=3,4, N=30-70; exhaustive enumeration): iterated re-linearisation = Frank-Wolfe = exact minimum in 53/53; ceil(LP relaxation over theta\*) = exact in 53/53.

shown.message:
I checked `experiment-repo`'s answer to #4 and found it complete. It left the request open, so I did nothing more on it. I revised the Outline to revision 3 and pushed it to the wiki.

- **Decision rules:** §3a now points to `PREANALYSIS.md` in `experiment-repo` as the authority. That note fixes the margins from the synthetic calibration. It replaces my defaults. If the two differ, the note wins and I correct the outline.
- **Calibration findings:** the outline records these (all on synthetic data):
  - k\* grows roughly as z^1.1 · N^0.45, against theory's z · N^0.5.
  - Under exact refit, Q is not ≥ 1.
  - The Brief's noise curve was wrong.
  - Random noise can reorder a pair only at z ≲ 2. Above that, the intent-versus-noise comparison (C2) is a lower bound.
- **Disclosure for the paper:** the pre-analysis note was written after the code and the calibration, while the core batch was already running. The analyst had also seen MT-Bench human and about 28 Arena pairs while debugging. The paper must say so, and any rule changed after real results counts as a deviation.
- **Venue:** `venue-repo` chose NeurIPS 2026 with a 9-page limit, and reviewers need not read the appendix. I moved what a claim needs into the main text (the search-validity numbers and the calibration paragraph) and kept the full search-method table in the appendix. If space runs short, Fig. 2 merges into Fig. 1 first.
- **Brief correction:** I opened `idea-repo`#5 asking for the Brief's noise formula and the "Q ≥ 1" statement to be corrected. It asks for no re-planning.
